items.q: A 7-year-old with PSGN has a BP of 150/100 mmHg. According to the treatment table, the drug of choice and its dose are:
opts: A calcium channel blocker — amlodipine 2.5–5 mg, with hourly BP charting
An ACE inhibitor — ramipril 5 mg once daily
A thiazide — chlorothiazide 250 mg twice daily
A beta blocker — metoprolol 25 mg twice daily
items.exp: Hypertension in PSGN: calcium channel blockers (amlodipine 2.5–5 mg) with BP charting hourly. (Book p776)

items.q: The amlodipine dose printed in the PSGN treatment table is:
items.exp: Hypertension in PSGN is treated with the CCB amlodipine 2.5–5 mg, with BP charted hourly. (Book p776)

items.q: A child with acute PSGN develops pulmonary oedema. The table's treatment is:
opts: Fluid restriction alone with no diuretic
items.exp: Pulmonary oedema in PSGN: diuretics, such as torsemide 5–10 mg. (Book p776)

items.q: The listed dose of torsemide for pulmonary oedema in PSGN is:
items.exp: Pulmonary oedema in PSGN is treated with diuretics — torsemide 5–10 mg. (Book p776)

items.q: A child with PSGN has a serum potassium of 6.6 mEq/L. Per the treatment table, the monitoring that must accompany this is:
opts: ECG monitoring to look for tall T waves, with regular serum K⁺ measurement
Weekly serum potassium testing alone is sufficient
items.exp: Hyperkalaemia (which can cause cardiac complications) in PSGN: ECG monitoring — check for tall T waves — and serum K⁺ checked regularly. (Book p776)

items.q: Match each sign in the PSGN treatment table with its prescription — 1) Hypertension  2) Pulmonary oedema  3) Hyperkalaemia … A) Torsemide 5–10 mg  B) ECG monitoring and serial serum K⁺  C) Amlodipine 2.5–5 mg with hourly BP charting
items.exp: Treatment table: hypertension → CCB amlodipine 2.5–5 mg + hourly BP charting; pulmonary oedema → diuretic torsemide 5–10 mg; hyperkalaemia → ECG monitoring (tall T waves) + regular serum K⁺. (Book p776)

items.q: The ECG change specifically named for hyperkalaemia in the PSGN treatment table is the tall T wave.
opts: False — the table names U waves
False — the table names a short PR interval
items.exp: Hyperkalaemia row: ECG monitoring (check for tall T waves) and serum K⁺ levels checked regularly. (Book p776)

items.q: The histopathology figure labelled 'DPGN histopathology' on this page illustrates:
opts: A hypercellular glomerulus from diffuse proliferative glomerulonephritis
A glomerulus with segmental sclerosis and hyalinosis
A glomerulus with spikes along the subepithelial space
A normal glomerulus with thin basement membranes
items.exp: The figure shows a light-microscopy image of DPGN (diffuse proliferative GN) — the characteristic histopathology of PSGN. (Book p776)

items.q: An immunofluorescence image in a child with acute PSGN is reported as a 'starry sky pattern'. This corresponds to:
opts: Granular IgG ± C3 in capillary walls, more than in the mesangium
Linear IgG along the glomerular basement membrane
Mesangial IgA with C3 in a garland pattern
Extensive crescent formation with fibrinogen staining
items.exp: Clinical-phase IF in PSGN: granular IgG ± C3 in capillary walls > mesangium, described as the starry sky pattern (figure 'IF: starry sky pattern'). (Book p776)

items.q: Which immunofluorescence pattern is NOT part of the described PSGN findings?
opts: Granular IgG ± C3 in capillary walls in the clinical phase
Only mesangial C3 in the recovery phase
items.exp: Linear IgG along the GBM indicates anti-GBM (Goodpasture/RPGN type I) disease, not PSGN, whose IF is granular in the clinical phase and mesangial C3-only in recovery. (Book p776)
